B. Is this measure already running in North Ostrobothnia wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In the Netherlands the share of elderly stage I patients left untreated fell by 7 percentage points once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available. That gain is among a subgroup only, so the effect on the share of all patients is indirect.
supported_en: Netherlands Cancer Registry data (Annals of Oncology 2012): 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated, with median survival 8 months longer.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the 0.8-point gain in the share of all patients treated to cure, and they do not show how many patients at OYS go untreated today.
in_use_quote: Paikallisessa tai paikallisesti edenneessä taudissa, jos leikkaushoito ei ole mahdollista, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa tai yhtä aikaa säde- ja solunsalpaajahoitoa eli kemosädehoitoa.
in_use_summary_en: OYS's lung cancer pathway page (updated 2025) says that when surgery is not possible for local disease, precision radiotherapy (täsmäsädehoito) can be given, and that the university hospital is responsible for the multidisciplinary meetings and for surgery and radiotherapy.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every stage I patient too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy, or any check that this happens.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer pathway page says precision radiotherapy can be given to local disease that cannot be operated, and that the university hospital runs the team meetings, surgery and radiotherapy; it does not describe a rule that refers every frail stage I patient. In a Netherlands registry study, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available. That supports the direction of our assumption, but only indirectly supports its size for all patients.
unanswered_en: No page showed a written referral rule at OYS or how many frail stage I patients there go untreated.
